OCR noise on a late 'Total Amt Rounded' line can inject a bogus number (e.g. 702.00 vs true 102.00 on 074.jpg) that dominates."},{"id":"RC2","description":"The number regex accepts single-decimal fragments (e.g. '88.1') produced by OCR truncation and formats them as '88.10', masking that the digit was dropped. No preference is given to candidates with exactly two decimal places matching typical monetary formatting."},{"id":"RC3","description":"Dual OCR variants are run sequentially but the first-non-null result wins; the agent never compares candidate quality (tier, decimal precision, agreement across variants) across both passes."},{"id":"RC4","description":"Ambiguous DD/MM vs MM/DD dates are resolved by first-matching pattern order rather than by locale/context (receipts from Malaysia overwhelmingly use DD/MM/YYYY). '09/03/2018' on 034.jpg was parsed as 2018-08-09 instead of 2018-03-09."},{"id":"RC5","description":"Missing/failed extractions are written as empty string in the xlsx cell rather than a true null/blank, violating the task's 'value is set to null' contract (078.jpg total_amount)."},{"id":"RC6","description":"Keyword priority tiering, exclusion-list handling, and two-line fallback are correctly described in the Skill but the Skill does not warn about the two highest-impact pitfalls above (OCR-truncated decimals, cross-variant disagreement, DD/MM default, null-vs-empty-cell)."}],"skill_defects":[{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Receipt total-extraction guidance tells the agent to format `f\"{v:.2f}\"` on any matched decimal number, with no rule preferring candidates whose raw OCR text already has exactly two decimal digits. This silently promotes truncated OCR like '88.1' to '88.10'."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"The 'critical rules' section recommends taking the FIRST match top-to-bottom OR last, 'depending on receipt convention — test on sample'. This hedging produced the wrong choice on 074.jpg where a later OCR-noised 'Total Amt Rounded' line was selected over an earlier clean 'Total incl. of GST'."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"No guidance on cross-validating the chosen total against other numbers on the receipt (subtotal, cash tendered minus change, repeated amounts) to filter out OCR hallucinations."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Multi-pass OCR section does not define a merge/vote strategy: when default and preprocessed OCR disagree, the Skill does not say to prefer the candidate from the higher priority tier, or with two-decimal precision, or with agreement across variants."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"Date extraction patterns list ISO-like `YYYY-MM-DD` first, then DD/MM/YYYY, then DMY-month-name. For Malaysian/receipt corpora the Skill should state DD/MM/YYYY is the default interpretation for ambiguous all-numeric dates and MM/DD only applies when the first field exceeds 12."},{"skill":"image-ocr","defect":"The 'Null on failure' bullet says to set the field to Python None, but gives no concrete pandas/openpyxl guidance; the resulting xlsx wrote an empty string for 078.jpg, which fails exact-equality scoring if the oracle expects a blank cell / NaN. Needs explicit instruction: write None via pandas with dtype=object and verify the written cell is empty (no inherited '' string) before saving."},{"skill":"xlsx","defect":"Does not document the convention for 'missing value' when writing a mixed string/null column: nothing warns the agent that `df.loc[i,'col']=''` is NOT equivalent to `None`, and that openpyxl renders '' as a non-empty cell. For OCR/extraction tasks this is the dominant source of null-mismatch errors."},{"skill":"xlsx","defect":"No guidance on preserving string formatting (e.g. '47.70' not float 47.7) when a column is written with pandas; the current wording about dtype=object is only in the image-ocr Skill, not cross-referenced from xlsx."}],"repair_recommendations":[{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"In the 'Total Amount Extraction' section, change NUM_RE to require exactly two decimal digits for monetary candidates (`\\d{1,3}(?:,\\d{3})*\\.\\d{2}` or `\\d+\\.\\d{2}`), and keep a secondary looser regex only as a fallback when no 2-decimal candidate exists in any tier. State explicitly: 'Never promote a 1-decimal OCR fragment like \"88.1\" to \"88.10\"; prefer another candidate with full two-decimal precision from the same or lower-priority tier, or from an alternative OCR variant.'"},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Replace the hedge 'first or last match depending on receipt convention' with a deterministic rule: within a priority tier, scan top-to-bottom and keep ALL candidates; pick the candidate value that (a) appears with exactly 2 decimal digits, (b) is corroborated by at least one other line on the receipt (subtotal, cash, rounded total, item total sum), and (c) is nearest in position to the matched keyword. Only fall back to 'last number on next line' when the keyword line itself has no number."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Add a 'Cross-variant reconciliation' subsection: run at least two OCR passes (default PSM and preprocessed PSM 6). For each pass, extract (tier, value, raw_decimal_digits). Prefer: lower tier index > exact 2-decimal raw text > agreement between passes > variant with higher mean OCR confidence. Document the ordering as a short pseudocode block generalizable beyond receipts."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Rewrite Date Extraction: for all-numeric three-part dates, state the default is DD/MM/YYYY unless the first component is >12 (then MM/DD/YYYY) or the first component is a 4-digit year (then YYYY-MM-DD). Add a worked example resolving '09/03/2018' → '2018-03-09'. Keep month-name patterns unchanged."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Strengthen the 'Null on failure' rule into a dedicated 'Writing nulls to tabular output' subsection: assign Python None (not '', not 'None', not NaN strings), set the destination column dtype to object before writing, and after saving reopen the xlsx with openpyxl to assert that failed cells are truly empty (`cell.value is None`). Reference the companion xlsx Skill."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"Add a 'Pitfalls specific to receipt totals' bullet list covering: late OCR-noised 'Total Amt Rounded' lines, 'TOTAL' substring inside 'SUBTOTAL' (reinforce exclusion-first), currency letters attached to digits ('702.00A'), and OCR confusions 1↔7, 0↔O that commonly affect the leading digit of amounts; recommend sanity-check that the chosen total is consistent with item total sum when item lines are reliably extracted."},{"skill":"xlsx","change":"Add a short 'Writing missing values' section: distinguish None vs '' vs NaN; show the pandas idiom `df['col'] = df['col'].astype(object); df.loc[mask,'col'] = None`; and recommend post-write verification with openpyxl that cells meant to be null have `cell.value is None`. Make this generalize to any extraction-to-xlsx workflow."},{"skill":"xlsx","change":"Cross-reference the string-preservation rule for fixed-decimal monetary strings (e.g. '47.70'): dtype=object, format BEFORE writing, do not let pandas or openpyxl re-cast to float. Include a one-liner example."},{"skill":"image-ocr","change":"In the Quality Self-Check, add explicit checks: (a) every non-null monetary string matches `^\\d+(?:,\\d{3})*\\.\\d{2}$`; (b) every non-null date matches `^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$` with month in 1..12 and day in 1..31; (c) all null fields are Python None in the DataFrame and empty cells in the xlsx; (d) chosen total was NOT taken from an exclusion-keyword line even after OCR noise rewrote part of the keyword."}],"confidence":0.78}
